18	/// Why a remote read or action failed.
19	///
20	/// Deliberately NOT folded into `VCSError`: that enum is the backend-*read* taxonomy
21	/// (`lockContention`/`staleSnapshot`/`partialData`/…) and `WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)`
22	/// switches over it exhaustively to choose a sidebar badge. `.authRequired` has no sidebar badge and
23	/// no sensible answer there, so adding it would force a meaningless decision in a function that
24	/// currently has a principled one for every case. Same reasoning that put `CIResolution`/`PRResolution`
25	/// beside their resolver instead of in `VCSModels.swift`.
26	enum VCSRemoteFailure: Equatable, Sendable {
27	  /// `git`/`jj` not on PATH. Distinct from `VCSToolVersions`' floor check, which runs at launch —
28	  /// this is the same condition caught at the point of use.
29	  case toolMissing(String)
30	  case timedOut(VCSRemoteAction)
31	  /// Credentials were needed and none were available.
32	  case authRequired(String)
33	  /// The host's key isn't in `known_hosts`. `BatchMode=yes` turns what would be an interactive
34	  /// confirmation into this, so it needs its own copy — telling the user to configure a credential
35	  /// helper would be wrong advice.
36	  case hostKeyUnverified(String)
37	  case noRemote
38	  /// Push rejected (non-fast-forward). The engine NEVER force-pushes; the UI offers Pull.
39	  case rejected(String)
40	  /// git refused because tracked files would be overwritten.
41	  case dirtyWorkingTree(String)
42	  /// A failed or killed `git pull --rebase` left `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply` behind. The repo needs
43	  /// `git rebase --abort`, so the UI must offer that instead of a retry that will fail identically.
44	  case rebaseInProgress
45	  /// A repo lock was held — git `index.lock`/`packed-refs.lock`, or jj's `git_import_export.lock`.
46	  ///
47	  /// The payload is the lock file itself when we could find it on disk, and that distinction decides
48	  /// what the UI offers. **`nil` ⇒ transient contention**, so Retry is genuine: another command held the
49	  /// lock briefly and by the next click it is likely gone. **Non-nil ⇒ a lock file is sitting there
50	  /// right now**, and retrying fails identically every time — the same reasoning that makes
51	  /// `rebaseInProgress` offer Abort instead of Retry.
52	  ///
53	  /// A leftover lock is what a SIGKILLed git leaves: the runner escalates to `killTree` two seconds
54	  /// after SIGTERM, and SIGKILL cannot be caught, so git's own cleanup never runs.
55	  ///
56	  /// Workroom does NOT delete it. Whether a lock is truly abandoned or held by a git running right now
57	  /// is not knowable from outside the process — `lsof` can't be trusted for it, and removing a live
58	  /// lock corrupts the index — so this reports and explains, and the removal stays the user's call.
59	  /// That is also what git's own message tells you to do.
60	  case locked(VCSLockFile?)
61	  /// jj refused to rewrite a commit protected by `immutable_heads()` — reached by Pull, whose
62	  /// `jj rebase -b @` moves the whole branch containing `@`, and that branch usually contains a
63	  /// remote-tracked commit. Measured on jj 0.43 for a workroom based off a feature branch while trunk
64	  /// moved on: `Error: Commit 4c8e754829da is immutable`.
65	  ///
66	  /// Offers no retry, for `rebaseInProgress`'s reason: the destination doesn't change between clicks, so
67	  /// every retry fails identically. The real fix is remembering each workroom's own base instead of
68	  /// guessing `trunk()` — filed, not built.
69	  case immutableHistory(String)
70	  /// jj refuses to push a commit with an empty description, changes or not. This is the state a workroom
71	  /// sits in the moment you edit a file and before you write a message, so it is the most reachable
72	  /// failure on the push path, not an edge case. Measured: `Error: Won't push commit 050e657d3c36 since
73	  /// it has no description`.
74	  case needsDescription(String)
75	  case other(String)
76	}

200	/// The seam for VCS operations that **write** — remote state reads plus fetch/push/pull.
201	///
202	/// Separate from `VCSProviding` on purpose. That protocol's doc calls it "the single seam the app
203	/// **reads** VCS data through", and four resolvers construct providers freely and call them with no
204	/// gate. Putting `fetch` there would mean nothing structurally prevented a read path from firing a
205	/// network mutation — the opposite of what `JJSnapshotGate` exists to guarantee. Keeping writes on
206	/// their own protocol also gives the injected `StatusCommandRunning` a home: `GitProvider` and
207	/// `RustJJProvider` are stateless value types constructed at four call sites with nowhere to put one.
208	///
209	/// This is the growth surface for the rest of the VCS write phase (commit/amend, bookmark management,
210	/// the deep jj ops), which is why it's a protocol with a factory rather than one standalone resolver —
211	/// otherwise each later operation re-derives repo kind and wires its own runner.
212	protocol VCSWriting: Sendable {
213	  /// Everything the toolbar renders, as ONE coherent snapshot.
214	  func remoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteResolution
215	  func fetch(path: String, projectRoot: String, remote: String) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
216	  /// `anonymousRevision` is used only by jj, and only when `@` carries no bookmark: it is the revision
217	  /// the auto-created `push-<change-id>` bookmark will point at. Compute it with
218	  /// `CLIVCSWriter.jjPushRevision(hasChanges:hasDescription:)` — pushing a bare `@` fails when the
219	  /// working copy is empty and undescribed, which is the state a fresh workroom sits in. Ignored by git.
220	  func push(
221	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String, setUpstream: Bool,
222	    anonymousRevision: String
223	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
224	  func pullRebase(
225	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String,
226	    tracking: VCSTracking?
227	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
228	  /// Recover a workroom left mid-rebase. git only; a no-op for jj, whose rebase is atomic and
229	  /// `jj undo`-able.
230	  func abortRebase(path: String, projectRoot: String) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult
231	
232	  /// Record a commit. **Local**, unlike everything above it, so it takes no `remote` and never runs
233	  /// through `runNetwork` — but it lands here rather than on `VCSProviding` for the reason this
234	  /// protocol's own doc gives: writes belong behind the gate, and a read seam that could commit is
235	  /// exactly what that separation prevents.
236	  ///
237	  /// Always runs in the **workroom**, both backends. `opDirectory` records the measured bug where a
238	  /// jj write at the project root operated on the ROOT workspace's `@` and reported success; a
239	  /// commit at the root would publish the wrong workspace's work in the same way.
240	  func commit(path: String, projectRoot: String, request: VCSCommitRequest) async -> VCSCommitResult
241	
242	  /// Selected paths whose STAGED content a commit would silently discard, so the caller can confirm
243	  /// first. Empty when there is nothing at risk. See `CLIVCSWriter.stagedContentAtRisk`.
244	  func stagedContentAtRisk(path: String, files: [ChangedFile]) async -> [String]
245	}

254	  /// The writer for a repo, or a typed error for an unsupported path. Mirrors `provider(for:)`, and
255	  /// routes on the same `repoKind(at:)`.
256	  static func writer(
257	    for root: URL, runner: StatusCommandRunning = StatusCommandRunner(),
258	    makeProvider: @escaping @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding = { try VCS.provider(for: $0) },
259	    gate: JJSnapshotGate = .shared
260	  ) throws -> VCSWriting {
261	    switch repoKind(at: root) {
262	    case .jjColocated, .jjNonColocated:
263	      return CLIVCSWriter(vcs: "jj", runner: runner, makeProvider: makeProvider, gate: gate)
264	    case .plainGit:
265	      return CLIVCSWriter(vcs: "git", runner: runner, makeProvider: makeProvider, gate: gate)
266	    case .unsupported(let reason):
267	      throw VCSError.unsupportedRepo(reason)

272	/// `VCSWriting` over the real `git` / `jj` CLIs.
273	///
274	/// **Why the CLI and not the libraries.** SwiftGitX 0.4.0's `fetch`/`push` pass `NULL` for the options
275	/// struct that would carry `git_remote_callbacks.credentials`, so they have no credential path at all —
276	/// HTTPS authentication is impossible through them — and it has no `pull`. Shelling the real binaries
277	/// means the user's own credential helpers, SSH agent and config just work, which is the same bet the
278	/// status layer already makes with `gh`. jj has no Swift API for these at all.
279	///
280	/// Pure `static` arg-builders, parsers and classifiers carry all the semantics, so they are unit-tested
281	/// without spawning anything — the pattern `RustJJProvider.workingDiffArgs` established for exactly
282	/// this reason.
283	///
284	/// ```
285	///                 ┌──────────── every network op ────────────┐
286	///                 │ runNetwork: stdin=/dev/null, BatchMode,   │
287	///                 │ askpass off, SSH_AUTH_SOCK forwarded      │
288	///                 └────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
289	///                                      │
290	///                 ┌────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐
291	///                 │  JJSnapshotGate.run(projectRoot:)         │  git writes too
292	///                 │  NEVER re-enter for the same root         │
293	///                 └────────────────────┬─────────────────────┘
294	///                                      │
295	///     git ─────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────── jj
296	///  fetch → PROJECT ROOT (FETCH_HEAD    │   fetch → PROJECT ROOT (a workspace
297	///          is per-worktree; the root   │           has no .git)
298	///          is one shared answer)       │   push  → PROJECT ROOT (bookmarks are
299	///  push  → workroom                    │           repo-global)
300	///  pull  → root (fetch) + workroom     │   pull  → root (fetch) + workroom (rebase)
301	///  abort → workroom                    │
302	/// ```
303	struct CLIVCSWriter: VCSWriting, Sendable {
304	  /// `"git"` or `"jj"` — resolved once by `VCS.writer(for:)` so no method re-derives it.
305	  let vcs: String
306	  let runner: StatusCommandRunning
307	  /// For `currentRef` only. The app already has a canonical answer including jj `.ancestor` and git
308	  /// `.detached`; re-deriving it from `%(HEAD)` would lose both.
309	  let makeProvider: @Sendable (URL) throws -> VCSProviding
310	  /// Serializes writes per project root. Applied to **git** as well as jj: a project's workrooms are
311	  /// `git worktree add` worktrees sharing one `.git`, so a lock lost mid-`pull --rebase` can leave a
312	  /// workroom wedged in a rebase.
313	  let gate: JJSnapshotGate
314	
315	  var refTimeout: TimeInterval = 5
316	  var fetchTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
317	  var pushTimeout: TimeInterval = 120
318	  /// Generous because SIGKILLing a rebase is the one genuinely unsafe timeout here — it can leave
319	  /// `rebase-merge` behind. `classify` probes for that and reports `.rebaseInProgress`.
320	  var pullTimeout: TimeInterval = 300
321	  /// Deliberately generous, and deliberately NOT tuned down. A `pre-commit` hook that runs a linter
322	  /// or a test suite routinely takes minutes, and `StatusCommandRunner` escalates to `killTree` two
323	  /// seconds after SIGTERM — SIGKILL is uncatchable, so git's own cleanup never runs and an
324	  /// `index.lock` is left behind. Workroom deliberately never deletes that file (see
325	  /// `VCSRemoteFailure.locked`), so a too-short limit here would wedge every later commit *and*
326	  /// every status probe until the user removed it by hand. Killing a commit is categorically more
327	  /// dangerous than killing a fetch.
328	  var commitTimeout: TimeInterval = 600
329	
330	  // MARK: - Placement
331	
332	  /// Where an operation must run.
333	  ///
334	  /// **fetch always runs at the project root, for both backends.** For jj because a secondary
335	  /// workspace has no `.git` (the rule `WorkroomStatusResolver.ghProbeDirectory` already encodes for
336	  /// `gh`). For git because `FETCH_HEAD` is **per-worktree** — fetching inside a workroom would leave
337	  /// the project and every sibling workroom reading "never fetched" while their remote refs were
338	  /// perfectly fresh. At the root it's one fact every workroom of the project agrees on.
339	  ///
340	  /// **Everything except fetch runs in the workroom, including jj push.** It used to send jj push to the
341	  /// root on the grounds that bookmarks are repo-global. Bookmarks are — but `@` is not: it is
342	  /// WORKSPACE-scoped, resolved against the working directory. So `jj git push --change @` run at the root
343	  /// pushed the ROOT workspace's working copy and left the workroom's commit at home, while still
344	  /// returning `.ok` so the toolbar reported "Pushed to origin".
345	  ///
346	  /// Measured, root holding `ROOT-WORKSPACE-WORK` and workspace `wsA` holding `WORKROOM-WORK`: the push
347	  /// created `refs/heads/push-<root's change id>` carrying `ROOT-WORKSPACE-WORK`. Wrong commit published,
348	  /// the user's work never sent, success reported. `--bookmark` works from a secondary workspace too, so
349	  /// nothing needed the root.
350	  ///
351	  /// The integration test could not see this — it passes `path` and `projectRoot` as the same directory,
352	  /// which makes the two indistinguishable. `opDirectoryTests` now pins them as different.
353	  static func opDirectory(_ action: VCSRemoteAction, path: String, projectRoot: String) -> String {
354	    switch action {
355	    case .fetch: return projectRoot
356	    case .push, .pull, .abortRebase: return path
357	    }
358	  }
359	
360	  /// The **common** git directory for a path — the one shared by every worktree of the repo.
361	  ///
362	  /// `.git` is a directory in a normal repo and a FILE in a worktree, containing
363	  /// `gitdir: <repo>/.git/worktrees/<name>`. That per-worktree directory has its own `FETCH_HEAD`,
364	  /// `HEAD` and `index`, so reading `FETCH_HEAD` from it after fetching at the root finds nothing —
365	  /// the root's fetch wrote the root's copy. Stripping the `/worktrees/<name>` suffix gets the shared
366	  /// directory, which is where a root fetch's `FETCH_HEAD` actually lands.
367	  ///
368	  /// Pure string work, no subprocess: `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` is authoritative but costs a
369	  /// process for something two file reads answer.
370	  static func commonGitDir(at path: String) -> URL? {
371	    let dotGit = URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(".git")
372	    var isDir: ObjCBool = false
373	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: dotGit.path, isDirectory: &isDir) else {
374	      return nil
375	    }
376	    if isDir.boolValue { return dotGit }
377	    // A worktree's `.git` file: `gitdir: /abs/or/relative/path`.
378	    guard let contents = try? String(contentsOf: dotGit, encoding: .utf8) else { return nil }
379	    let line = contents.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).first.map(String.init) ?? ""
380	    guard line.hasPrefix("gitdir:") else { return nil }
381	    let raw = String(line.dropFirst("gitdir:".count)).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
382	    guard !raw.isEmpty else { return nil }
383	    let gitDir =
384	      raw.hasPrefix("/")
385	      ? URL(fileURLWithPath: raw)
386	      : URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(raw).standardized
387	    // `<common>/worktrees/<name>` → `<common>`.
388	    let parts = gitDir.standardized.pathComponents
389	    guard let index = parts.lastIndex(of: "worktrees"), index > 0 else { return gitDir }
390	    return URL(fileURLWithPath: "/" + parts[1..<index].joined(separator: "/"))
391	  }
392	
393	  /// `FETCH_HEAD`'s modification time. git rewrites it on **every** fetch, no-ops included (verified),
394	  /// so its mtime is a complete record of git fetches — including one the user ran in a terminal.
395	  static func gitLastFetch(commonGitDir: URL?) -> VCSLastFetch {
396	    guard let dir = commonGitDir else { return .unknown }
397	    let head = dir.appendingPathComponent("FETCH_HEAD")
398	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: head.path) else { return .never }
399	    guard
400	      let attrs = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: head.path),
401	      let date = attrs[.modificationDate] as? Date
402	    else { return .unknown }
403	    return .at(date)
404	  }

408	  /// Every remote ref plus, implicitly, the remote names. No `--count` cap: with branch switching cut
409	  /// there is no picker to fill, so this only ever answers "which remotes exist" and "does my branch
410	  /// have a counterpart".

412	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + [
413	      "for-each-ref", "--format=%(refname)%00%(objectname)%00%(symref)", "refs/remotes",
414	    ]

417	  /// The CONFIGURED remotes, one name per line.
418	  ///
419	  /// Deliberately separate from `gitRemoteRefsArgs`: remote-tracking refs prove a remote has been
420	  /// *fetched*, not that one is configured. `git remote add origin …` writes config and no refs, so a
421	  /// remotes list derived from `refs/remotes` reads as "No remote configured" on a repo that can push
422	  /// perfectly well. Config is the authority for "is there a remote"; the refs still answer "does my
423	  /// branch have a counterpart".
424	  static func gitRemoteListArgs() -> [String] {
425	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + ["remote"]
426	  }

428	  /// Exact two-way divergence, independent of the user's `push.default`.
429	  ///
430	  /// **Deliberately not `%(push:track)`/`%(upstream:track)`.** Under `push.default=simple` — git's
431	  /// built-in default — `%(push)` resolves to nothing for a branch with no upstream, and every
432	  /// workroom is `git worktree add -b`, i.e. has no upstream. Deriving counts from that field leaves
433	  /// the badge permanently blank on any machine not set to `push.default=current` (verified on git
434	  /// 2.55). It also sidesteps a branch whose `%(upstream)` is a *local* branch, which would otherwise
435	  /// produce counts against a ref that isn't on any remote.
436	  ///
437	  /// `A...B` with `--left-right --count` prints `<only in A>\t<only in B>`, so with `A = HEAD` the
438	  /// left number is ahead and the right is behind.
439	  static func gitCountsArgs(remote: String, branch: String) -> [String] {
440	    WorkroomStatusResolver.gitHardening + [
441	      "rev-list", "--left-right", "--count", "HEAD...refs/remotes/\(remote)/\(branch)",
442	    ]

518	  /// The NUL-separated pathspec payload for `--pathspec-from-file=-`, written to the child's stdin.
519	  ///
520	  /// Three things here are load-bearing, and all three were **measured** on git 2.x rather than
521	  /// reasoned about:
522	  ///
523	  /// 1. **A rename contributes BOTH sides.** `ChangedFile` carries `oldPath`, and the status layer
524	  ///    pairs renames (`.renamesIndex`/`.renamesWorkingTree`), so one row means two paths. Sending
525	  ///    only `path`: `mv old new` then committing `new` recorded an **add** and left `D old`
526	  ///    dangling in the worktree — staged, if the rename came from `git mv`. The user ticked one row
527	  ///    labelled `old → new` and got half a rename plus a mess.
528	  ///
529	  /// 2. **Every entry is `:(literal)`-prefixed.** `--` ends OPTION parsing, not MAGIC parsing, and
530	  ///    `--pathspec-file-nul` does NOT disable globbing either — its "taken literally" refers to the
531	  ///    absence of C-quoting in the file format, not to pathspec magic. Measured with `ab.txt` and
532	  ///    `a[b].txt` both modified: sending `a[b].txt` committed BOTH. A file named `*` would commit
533	  ///    the whole tree. `:(literal)` is what actually turns it off (verified: commits only the
534	  ///    bracketed file), and it still parses under `--pathspec-file-nul`.
535	  ///
536	  /// 3. **NUL separation, so no path needs escaping** — newlines and quotes in filenames pass
537	  ///    through unharmed, and thousands of long paths cannot blow the `E2BIG` argv ceiling at spawn,
538	  ///    where git would never get to emit anything classifiable.
539	  ///
540	  /// Order-preserving dedup: a rename whose `oldPath` is also its own `path` (or two rows naming the
541	  /// same file) must not send a duplicate.
542	  static func gitPathspecPayload(_ files: [ChangedFile]) -> Data {
543	    var seen = Set<String>()
544	    var out = Data()
545	    for file in files {
546	      for path in [file.path, file.oldPath].compactMap({ $0 }) where !path.isEmpty {
547	        guard seen.insert(path).inserted else { continue }
548	        out.append(contentsOf: Array(":(literal)\(path)".utf8))
549	        out.append(0)
550	      }
551	    }
552	    return out
553	  }

555	  /// The same payload, from paths that are already just paths.
556	  ///
557	  /// Used by the intent-to-add step, which must send **only the new side** of a rename. The old side
558	  /// no longer exists on disk, and `git add` rejects a pathspec matching nothing — `fatal: pathspec
559	  /// ':(literal)old.txt' did not match any files` — which would fail the whole commit at the step
560	  /// meant to make it possible. `commit --only` is the opposite: it needs both sides, so the two
561	  /// steps deliberately do not share a payload.
562	  static func gitPathspecPayload(literalPaths: [String]) -> Data {
563	    var seen = Set<String>()
564	    var out = Data()
565	    for path in literalPaths where !path.isEmpty {
566	      guard seen.insert(path).inserted else { continue }
567	      out.append(contentsOf: Array(":(literal)\(path)".utf8))
568	      out.append(0)
569	    }
570	    return out
571	  }

631	  /// accept `--pathspec-from-file` (measured: `error: invalid option`), and passing thousands of
632	  /// paths as argv is the `E2BIG` problem the commit path avoids. One unfiltered read plus an

638	  /// Which of `paths` hold staged content that committing would DISCARD.
639	  ///
640	  /// `git commit --only` builds the commit from the **worktree**, so for a selected path whose index
641	  /// differs from both HEAD and the worktree, the staged intermediate is bypassed and then lost.
642	  /// That is precisely what someone who ran `git add -p` has: a half-staged file they are still
643	  /// editing. Measured — the staged hunk vanished with a clean `git status` afterwards and no warning.
644	  ///
645	  /// Porcelain's two columns already encode it, so no extra command is needed:
646	  /// `X` is HEAD→index and `Y` is index→worktree, giving `MM f.txt` (at risk), `M  h.txt` (staged and
647	  /// identical to disk — safe) and ` M g.txt` (never staged — safe). `?` is untracked, which has no
648	  /// staged state to lose.
649	  ///
650	  /// Pure, so the whole rule is testable without a repo.
651	  static func stagedContentAtRisk(porcelainZ: String, selecting paths: Set<String>) -> [String] {
652	    var atRisk: [String] = []
653	    var fields = porcelainZ.split(separator: "\0", omittingEmptySubsequences: true).map(String.init)
654	    var index = 0
655	    while index < fields.count {
656	      let entry = fields[index]
657	      index += 1
658	      guard entry.count > 3 else { continue }
659	      let chars = Array(entry)
660	      let x = chars[0]
661	      let y = chars[1]
662	      let path = String(chars[3...])
663	      // A rename or copy spends a SECOND field on its old path. Consuming it keeps the walk aligned;
664	      // without this every entry after the first rename would be read as a status code.
665	      if x == "R" || x == "C" { index += 1 }
666	      guard paths.contains(path) else { continue }
667	      // Staged content exists (X is neither unmodified nor untracked) AND the worktree has moved on
668	      // from it (Y is not unmodified) ⇒ `--only` will take the worktree copy and drop the staged one.
669	      if x != " " && x != "?" && y != " " { atRisk.append(path) }
670	    }
671	    return atRisk
672	  }

886	  /// Parse `for-each-ref refs/remotes` output.
887	  ///
888	  /// Skips records with a non-empty `%(symref)` — that's `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD`, whose short
889	  /// name is the bare remote and which would otherwise look like a branch called `origin`.
890	  /// Field count is checked rather than assumed: a ref name can't contain a control character, but
891	  /// being strict here means a malformed line is dropped rather than crashing the read.
892	  static func parseGitRemoteRefs(_ stdout: String) -> RemoteRefs {
893	    var remotes: [String] = []
894	    var shortNames: Set<String> = []
895	    for line in stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) {
896	      let fields = line.components(separatedBy: "\0")
897	      guard fields.count == 3 else { continue }
898	      guard fields[2].isEmpty else { continue }  // symref → origin/HEAD
899	      let refname = fields[0]
900	      let prefix = "refs/remotes/"
901	      guard refname.hasPrefix(prefix) else { continue }
902	      let short = String(refname.dropFirst(prefix.count))
903	      guard let slash = short.firstIndex(of: "/") else { continue }
904	      let remote = String(short[short.startIndex..<slash])
905	      guard !remote.isEmpty, slash < short.index(before: short.endIndex) else { continue }
906	      if !remotes.contains(remote) { remotes.append(remote) }
907	      shortNames.insert(short)
908	    }
909	    return RemoteRefs(remotes: remotes, shortNames: shortNames)
910	  }

958	  /// Parse `bookmark list --all-remotes` output into per-name tracking, plus the remote names.
959	  ///
960	  /// **jj's counts are inverted relative to git and are swapped here.** `tracking_ahead_count()` on an
961	  /// `@origin` ref means *the remote is ahead of local*, which is git's **behind** — jj's own default
962	  /// template proves it by printing "ahead by N commits" next to `@origin`. One line, one comment, and
963	  /// a cross-backend integration test pins it.
964	  static func parseJJBookmarks(_ stdout: String) -> (bookmarks: [JJBookmark], remotes: [String]) {
965	    var remotes: [String] = []
966	    var trackingByName: [String: VCSTracking] = [:]
967	    var localNames: [String] = []
968	    for line in stdout.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) {
969	      let f = line.components(separatedBy: "\0")
970	      guard f.count == 8 else { continue }
971	      let (name, remote) = (f[0], f[1])
972	      let present = f[3] == "1"
973	      let tracked = f[5] == "1"
974	      guard !name.isEmpty else { continue }
975	      if remote.isEmpty {
976	        if !localNames.contains(name) { localNames.append(name) }
977	        continue
978	      }
979	      // A colocated repo exposes a pseudo-remote called `git` (jj's local git-tracking bookmarks).
980	      // It is not a remote, and including it would both pollute the remote list and produce counts
981	      // against the local git refs rather than a server.
982	      guard remote != "git" else { continue }
983	      if !remotes.contains(remote) { remotes.append(remote) }
984	      // An untracked remote bookmark, or one deleted on the remote, cannot answer counts. `gone`
985	      // reports the deletion; nil counts report "unanswerable" rather than a misleading zero.
986	      let jjAhead = Int(f[6])
987	      let jjBehind = Int(f[7])
988	      trackingByName[name] = VCSTracking(
989	        comparedTo: "\(name)@\(remote)",
990	        ahead: tracked && present ? jjBehind : nil,  // swapped — see the doc comment
991	        behind: tracked && present ? jjAhead : nil,
992	        gone: !present)
993	    }
994	    let bookmarks = localNames.map { JJBookmark(name: $0, tracking: trackingByName[$0]) }
995	    return (bookmarks, remotes)
996	  }

1018	  /// Map a failed command to a typed failure. `nil` means success.
1019	  ///
1020	  /// `gitDir` lets a failed pull be upgraded to `.rebaseInProgress` — the distinction matters because
1021	  /// that state must offer Abort, not Retry.
1022	  static func classify(
1023	    _ result: CommandResult, action: VCSRemoteAction, tool: String,
1024	    gitDir: URL? = nil
1025	  ) -> VCSRemoteFailure? {
1026	    if result.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .toolMissing(tool) }
1027	    let err = result.stderr + "\n" + result.stdout
1028	    // A timed-out pull may have left a rebase behind; that reads better than "timed out".
1029	    if result.timedOut {
1030	      if action == .pull, rebaseInProgress(gitDir: gitDir) { return .rebaseInProgress }
1031	      return .timedOut(action)
1032	    }
1033	    guard !result.ok else { return nil }
1034	    if err.contains("Host key verification failed") || err.contains("REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION") {
1035	      return .hostKeyUnverified(err)
1036	    }
1037	    if err.contains("terminal prompts disabled") || err.contains("could not read Username")
1038	      || err.contains("could not read Password") || err.contains("Authentication failed")
1039	      || err.contains("Permission denied (publickey)")
1040	    {
1041	      return .authRequired(err)
1042	    }
1043	    if err.contains("would be overwritten") { return .dirtyWorkingTree(err) }
1044	    if err.contains("does not appear to be a git repository") || err.contains("No such remote")
1045	      || err.contains("no such remote") || err.contains("No git remotes")
1046	    {
1047	      return .noRemote
1048	    }
1049	    // Flag column first, prose second. The string checks stay as a fallback rather than being replaced:
1050	    // `--porcelain` is ours to pass on the push path only, so a rejection surfaced by any other route
1051	    // (a remote helper, a future caller that forgets the flag) still classifies.
1052	    if gitPushRejected(stdout: result.stdout) || err.contains("Updates were rejected")
1053	      || err.contains("! [rejected]")
1054	    {
1055	      return .rejected(err)
1056	    }
1057	    // Both jj-only, and both permanent until the user acts — so they must NOT reach `.other`, whose
1058	    // recovery is a retry of the same doomed command. jj doesn't localize, so matching its prose is safe
1059	    // here in a way it wouldn't be for git.
1060	    if err.contains("since it has no description") || err.contains("has no description") {
1061	      return .needsDescription(err)
1062	    }
1063	    if err.contains("is immutable") || err.contains("immutable commits") {
1064	      return .immutableHistory(err)
1065	    }
1066	    if err.contains("Failed to take lock for Git import/export")
1067	      || (err.contains(".lock")
1068	        && (err.contains("could not be obtained") || err.contains("File exists")
1069	          || err.contains("Unable to create")))
1070	    {
1071	      return .locked(lockFile(in: err))
1072	    }
1073	    if action == .pull, rebaseInProgress(gitDir: gitDir) { return .rebaseInProgress }
1074	    // A lock failure that never names a lock. git's message depends on WHICH internal step hit the lock:
1075	    // a fast-forward pull reports `Unable to create '<path>': File exists.`, but a pull that must really
1076	    // rebase fails in autostash first and says only `error: could not write index` / `fatal: Cannot
1077	    // autostash` — no path, no "lock", nothing the checks above can match. That is the diverged pull,
1078	    // i.e. exactly what the toolbar's Pull button is for, and it was landing in `.other` with raw stderr.
1079	    //
1080	    // So when the symptoms are lock-shaped, ask the DISK instead of the message. Deliberately last: any
1081	    // failure git explains properly keeps its own classification, and this only speaks for the ones it
1082	    // doesn't.
1083	    if lockSymptom(err), let lock = existingLockFile(gitDir: gitDir) { return .locked(lock) }
1084	    let trimmed = err.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
1085	    return .other(trimmed.isEmpty ? "\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)" : trimmed)
1086	  }

1114	  /// (@-)` lines, so a `contains` here would fire on any commit whose own message happened to carry
1115	  /// the phrase — reporting a successful write as a no-op.

1118	  /// nothing and survives jj moving it.

1131	  /// relabel signing failures, bad config, index corruption and message-policy errors as "a hook
1132	  /// rejected this", which is worse than saying nothing: it sends the user to edit a hook that was
1133	  /// never involved. Anything unmatched stays `.other`, carrying git's own words.
1134	  static let commitHookMarkers = [

1136	    "hook exited with", "hook returned",

1139	  /// Map a failed commit to a typed failure. `nil` means success.
1140	  ///
1141	  /// `movedRef` says the ref changed even though the command reported failure — the caller turns
1142	  /// that into `.committedThenFailed` rather than a failure, because retrying would make a SECOND
1143	  /// commit. The reachable case is a `post-commit` hook: git has already written the commit and
1144	  /// moved `HEAD` by the time it runs, so a hook that fails or runs past the timeout leaves a
1145	  /// perfectly good commit behind a non-zero exit.
1146	  static func classifyCommit(_ result: CommandResult, tool: String) -> VCSCommitFailure? {
1147	    if result.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .toolMissing(tool) }
1148	    // jj says "Nothing changed." and exits ZERO, so its no-op has to be read BEFORE the success
1149	    // guard — an untouched working copy must not be reported as a commit that happened.
1150	    //
1151	    // Scoped to jj, matched on a whole stderr line, and never against stdout. All three matter:
1152	    // `git commit` echoes the SUBJECT on stdout, so the substring form this replaces classified
1153	    // `-m "explain the nothing to commit error"` — a commit that succeeded, exit 0 — as a failure,
1154	    // and `commit()` then upgraded it to `.committedThenFailed` because the ref had legitimately
1155	    // moved. The dialog told the user their commit had half-worked when it was perfect. jj puts
1156	    // everything on stderr including its own echo of the description (`Parent commit (@-) … <msg>`),
1157	    // hence the whole-line anchor rather than `contains`. Measured on git 2.55 / jj 0.43.
1158	    if tool == "jj", result.ok, saysNothingChanged(result) { return .nothingToCommit }
1159	    if result.timedOut { return .timedOut }
1160	    guard !result.ok else { return nil }
1161	
1162	    // Only now, on a genuine failure, is matching the combined output safe: git's own
1163	    // "nothing to commit, working tree clean" goes to stdout with a non-zero exit.
1164	    let err = result.stderr + "\n" + result.stdout
1165	    if commitNothingMarkers.contains(where: err.contains) { return .nothingToCommit }
1166	    if commitIdentityMarkers.contains(where: err.contains) { return .identityMissing(err) }
1167	    if commitSigningMarkers.contains(where: err.contains) { return .signingFailed(err) }
1168	    if commitUnmergedMarkers.contains(where: err.contains) { return .unmergedFiles(err) }
1169	    // Before the hook check: git phrases this one as a plain fatal, and it is a state the user must
1170	    // finish rather than a hook they must fix.
1171	    if err.contains("cannot do a partial commit during a") || err.contains("is in progress") {
1172	      return .sequencerInProgress(err)
1173	    }
1174	    if commitHookMarkers.contains(where: err.contains) { return .hookRejected(err) }
1175	    if err.contains("Failed to take lock") || err.contains("index.lock")
1176	      || (err.contains(".lock")
1177	        && (err.contains("could not be obtained") || err.contains("File exists")
1178	          || err.contains("Unable to create")))
1179	    {
1180	      return .locked(lockFile(in: err))
1181	    }
1182	    let trimmed = err.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
1183	    return .other(trimmed.isEmpty ? "\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)" : trimmed)
1184	  }

1278	  /// The quoted path out of git's lock errors. Pure, so the parsing is testable without a repo.
1279	  ///
1280	  /// Covers both phrasings that quote a path — the bare `Unable to create '<path>'` and the ref-update
1281	  /// form (`error: cannot lock ref 'refs/…': Unable to create '<path>.lock': File exists`), which nests
1282	  /// two quoted strings and must yield the second.
1283	  static func parseLockPath(_ stderr: String) -> String? {
1284	    guard let marker = stderr.range(of: "Unable to create '") else { return nil }
1285	    let rest = stderr[marker.upperBound...]
1286	    guard let close = rest.firstIndex(of: "'") else { return nil }
1287	    let path = String(rest[..<close])
1288	    // Only ever report an absolute path to a `.lock`: a relative one would be meaningless to a user
1289	    // reading it out of a tooltip, and a non-`.lock` match means the phrasing wasn't what we assumed.
1290	    guard path.hasPrefix("/"), path.hasSuffix(".lock") else { return nil }
1291	    return path
1292	  }

1294	  /// This worktree's OWN git directory — `<common>/worktrees/<name>` for a workroom, the same as the
1295	  /// common dir for a project root. Rebase state (`rebase-merge`), `HEAD` and `index` live here, unlike
1296	  /// `FETCH_HEAD` which `commonGitDir` deliberately resolves to the shared copy.
1297	  static func worktreeGitDir(at path: String) -> URL? {
1298	    let dotGit = URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(".git")
1299	    var isDir: ObjCBool = false
1300	    guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: dotGit.path, isDirectory: &isDir) else {
1301	      return nil
1302	    }
1303	    if isDir.boolValue { return dotGit }
1304	    guard let contents = try? String(contentsOf: dotGit, encoding: .utf8) else { return nil }
1305	    let line = contents.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).first.map(String.init) ?? ""
1306	    guard line.hasPrefix("gitdir:") else { return nil }
1307	    let raw = String(line.dropFirst("gitdir:".count)).trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
1308	    guard !raw.isEmpty else { return nil }
1309	    return raw.hasPrefix("/")
1310	      ? URL(fileURLWithPath: raw)
1311	      : URL(fileURLWithPath: path, isDirectory: true).appendingPathComponent(raw).standardized
1312	  }

1353	  private func gitRemoteState(path: String, current: VCSRef) async -> VCSRemoteResolution {
1354	    let refs = await run(Self.gitRemoteRefsArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
1355	    if let failure = Self.classify(refs, action: .fetch, tool: "git") {
1356	      // A blip must not blank a good toolbar; a missing tool or a real error should show.
1357	      if case .timedOut = failure { return .keepPrior }
1358	      return .failed(failure)
1359	    }
1360	    let parsed = Self.parseGitRemoteRefs(refs.stdout)
1361	    let list = await run(Self.gitRemoteListArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
1362	    let remotes = Self.mergeRemotes(
1363	      configured: list.ok ? Self.parseGitRemoteList(list.stdout) : [], derived: parsed.remotes)
1364	    let primary = Self.primaryRemote(remotes)
1365	    var tracking: VCSTracking?
1366	    if let primary, let branch = current.name, current.kind == .branch {
1367	      let counterpart = "\(primary)/\(branch)"
1368	      if parsed.shortNames.contains(counterpart) {
1369	        let counts = await run(
1370	          Self.gitCountsArgs(remote: primary, branch: branch), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
1371	        if let parsedCounts = Self.parseCounts(counts.stdout) {
1372	          tracking = VCSTracking(
1373	            comparedTo: counterpart, ahead: parsedCounts.ahead, behind: parsedCounts.behind,
1374	            gone: false)
1375	        } else {
1376	          tracking = VCSTracking(comparedTo: counterpart, ahead: nil, behind: nil, gone: false)
1377	        }
1378	      } else {
1379	        // No counterpart on the remote — the normal state of a fresh workroom, since
1380	        // `git worktree add -b` sets no upstream. Reported as `gone` so the toolbar offers Publish.
1381	        tracking = VCSTracking(comparedTo: counterpart, ahead: nil, behind: nil, gone: true)
1382	      }
1383	    }
1384	    return .state(
1385	      VCSRemoteState(
1386	        current: current, tracking: tracking, remotes: remotes, primaryRemote: primary,
1387	        lastFetch: Self.gitLastFetch(commonGitDir: Self.commonGitDir(at: path)),
1388	        resolvedAt: Date()))
1389	  }

1391	  private func jjRemoteState(path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef) async
1392	    -> VCSRemoteResolution
1393	  {
1394	    // Reads take no lock, so they stay ungated.
1395	    let list = await run(Self.jjBookmarkListArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
1396	    if let failure = Self.classify(list, action: .fetch, tool: "jj") {
1397	      if case .timedOut = failure { return .keepPrior }
1398	      return .failed(failure)
1399	    }
1400	    let parsed = Self.parseJJBookmarks(list.stdout)
1401	    let remoteList = await run(Self.jjRemoteListArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
1402	    let remotes = Self.mergeRemotes(
1403	      configured: remoteList.ok ? Self.parseJJRemoteList(remoteList.stdout) : [],
1404	      derived: parsed.remotes)
1405	    let primary = Self.primaryRemote(remotes)
1406	    var tracking: VCSTracking?
1407	    if let primary {
1408	      switch current.kind {
1409	      case .branch:
1410	        if let name = current.name {
1411	          // No `@<remote>` row for this bookmark ⇒ it has never been pushed. Reported as `gone`, exactly
1412	          // as the git path reports a missing counterpart, so the toolbar offers Publish. Leaving it nil
1413	          // fell through to the fetch tier, which offered a Fetch that can never produce the counterpart
1414	          // — the permanent dead end a freshly-remoted repo landed in.
1415	          tracking =
1416	            parsed.bookmarks.first { $0.name == name }?.tracking
1417	            ?? VCSTracking(
1418	              comparedTo: "\(name)@\(primary)", ahead: nil, behind: nil, gone: true)
1419	        }
1420	      // `.none` belongs with `.ancestor`, and leaving it out was a bug that hid the exact case this
1421	      // toolbar exists for. `jj git fetch` fast-forwards a tracked local bookmark, so as soon as the
1422	      // main line moves, an unbookmarked `@`'s ancestry contains no bookmark at all and `currentRef`
1423	      // drops from `.ancestor` to `.none`. Sending that to `tracking = nil` meant the counts, the pills
1424	      // and `canPull` all vanished at the moment the workroom first became behind — the toolbar went
1425	      // quiet precisely when it had something to say. The revsets below never needed a bookmark to
1426	      // begin with; `.detached` still yields nil, since that's git's shape and has no jj meaning.
1427	      case .ancestor, .none:
1428	        // `@` carries no bookmark — the normal workroom state, since `jj workspace add --name` creates
1429	        // no bookmark. The bookmark row's counts would describe the ANCESTOR, not the user's work, so
1430	        // count the actual revsets instead. The two are deliberately scoped differently: ahead against
1431	        // every remote bookmark (anything already pushed anywhere isn't ahead), behind against `trunk()`
1432	        // alone (see `jjBehindRevset` — the all-bookmarks form counted other branches' work as ours to
1433	        // pull). Both agree with what the buttons do: `jjPushRevision` and `jjRebaseDestination`.
1434	        let ahead = await run(
1435	          Self.jjRevsetCountArgs(Self.jjAheadRevset(remote: primary)), in: path, timeout: refTimeout
1436	        )
1437	        let behind = await run(
1438	          Self.jjRevsetCountArgs(Self.jjBehindRevset), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
1439	        tracking = VCSTracking(
1440	          comparedTo: primary,
1441	          ahead: ahead.ok ? Self.countLines(ahead.stdout) : nil,
1442	          behind: behind.ok ? Self.countLines(behind.stdout) : nil,
1443	          gone: false)
1444	      case .detached:
1445	        tracking = nil
1446	      }
1447	    }
1448	    // jj's fetch is invisible to `FETCH_HEAD` (it passes `--no-write-fetch-head`), so scan the op log.
1449	    let ops = await run(Self.jjOpLogArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
1450	    let lastFetch = ops.ok ? Self.parseJJFetchOp(ops.stdout) : nil
1451	    return .state(
1452	      VCSRemoteState(
1453	        current: current, tracking: tracking, remotes: remotes, primaryRemote: primary,
1454	        lastFetch: lastFetch.map { .at($0) } ?? (ops.ok ? .never : .unknown),
1455	        resolvedAt: Date()))
1456	  }

1532	  func pullRebase(
1533	    path: String, projectRoot: String, current: VCSRef, remote: String,
1534	    tracking: VCSTracking?
1535	  ) async -> VCSRemoteActionResult {
1536	    // Both backends fetch first, at the project root, for the reasons `opDirectory` documents. For git
1537	    // `pull` would fetch too, but doing it explicitly at the root keeps `FETCH_HEAD` — and so the
1538	    // "last fetched" label — correct for every workroom of the project.
1539	    // Hoisted above the fetch: BOTH steps classify against it, since a lock can block either one.
1540	    let gitDir = Self.worktreeGitDir(at: path)
1541	    let fetchDir = Self.opDirectory(.fetch, path: path, projectRoot: projectRoot)
1542	    let fetchArgs =
1543	      vcs == "jj" ? Self.jjFetchArgs(remote: remote) : Self.gitFetchArgs(remote: remote)
1544	    guard
1545	      let fetched = await gated(
1546	        projectRoot,
1547	        { [self] in
1548	          await run(fetchArgs, in: fetchDir, timeout: fetchTimeout, network: true)
1549	        })
1550	    else { return .failed(.other("pull was cancelled")) }
1551	    if let failure = Self.classify(fetched, action: .pull, tool: vcs, gitDir: gitDir) {
1552	      return .failed(failure)
1553	    }
1554	
1555	    let dir = Self.opDirectory(.pull, path: path, projectRoot: projectRoot)
1556	    let args: [String]
1557	    if vcs == "jj" {
1558	      // Always rebases now. An unbookmarked `@` falls back to `trunk()` rather than returning early:
1559	      // fetching moves the remote bookmarks but does NOT move `@`, so stopping there left the workroom
1560	      // as far behind as it started while the toolbar went on offering Pull. Already a descendant of the
1561	      // destination is not an error — jj prints "Nothing changed." and exits 0.
1562	      args = Self.jjRebaseArgs(
1563	        onto: Self.jjRebaseDestination(comparedTo: tracking?.comparedTo, remote: remote))
1564	    } else {
1565	      guard let branch = Self.pullBranch(current: current, tracking: tracking) else {
1566	        return .failed(.other("no remote branch to pull from."))
1567	      }
1568	      args = Self.gitPullArgs(remote: remote, branch: branch)
1569	    }
1570	    guard
1571	      let result = await gated(
1572	        projectRoot,
1573	        { [self] in
1574	          await run(args, in: dir, timeout: pullTimeout, network: true)
1575	        })
1576	    else { return .failed(.other("pull was cancelled")) }
1577	    if let failure = Self.classify(result, action: .pull, tool: vcs, gitDir: gitDir) {
1578	      return .failed(failure)
1579	    }

1611	  // MARK: - Commit
1612	
1613	  func commit(path: String, projectRoot: String, request: VCSCommitRequest) async -> VCSCommitResult
1614	  {
1615	    guard Self.supports(mode: request.mode, vcs: vcs) else { return .failed(.unsupportedMode) }
1616	    let gitDir = Self.worktreeGitDir(at: path)
1617	    // A parked merge/cherry-pick/rebase/bisect makes a path-limited commit outright invalid, and
1618	    // finishing it is the user's call. Checked before the ref snapshot so nothing is spawned at all.
1619	    if vcs != "jj", let sequencer = Self.sequencerState(gitDir: gitDir) {
1620	      return .failed(.sequencerInProgress(sequencer))
1621	    }
1622	
1623	    // ONE gate acquisition for the whole operation, not one per command. Two would let the 15s
1624	    // status sweep, the FSEvents lane and DiffResolver interleave between the intent-to-add and the
1625	    // commit — contending on `index.lock` and, for jj, snapshotting `@` out from under a write.
1626	    //
1627	    // `before` is read INSIDE the gate, not before acquiring it. Outside, anything that moves the ref
1628	    // while this call waits its turn — a queued status snapshot (which rewrites `@` for jj, so the op
1629	    // head moves on every one), another window, the user's own terminal during a slow hook — would
1630	    // make the before/after comparison below read a ref that moved for someone else's reason. A
1631	    // commit that genuinely failed would then be reported as `.committedThenFailed`, whose copy tells
1632	    // the user their work is saved and not to commit again. It would not be.
1633	    let outcome = await gated(
1634	      projectRoot,
1635	      { [self] in
1636	        let before = await currentRevision(path: path)
1637	        return CommitAttempt(before: before, result: await runCommitSequence(request, in: path))
1638	      })
1639	    guard let attempt = outcome else { return .failed(.other("commit was cancelled")) }
1640	    let (before, result) = (attempt.before, attempt.result)
1641	
1642	    if let failure = Self.classifyCommit(result, tool: vcs) {
1643	      // The command failed, but did the ref move anyway? A `post-commit` hook runs AFTER git has
1644	      // written the commit and moved HEAD, so a hook that fails — or that we killed at the timeout —
1645	      // leaves a real commit behind a non-zero exit. Reporting that as a plain failure invites a
1646	      // retry, and the retry would commit a second time.
1647	      let after = await currentRevision(path: path)
1648	      if let after, after != before {
1649	        return .committedThenFailed(revision: after, detail: Self.commitFailureDetail(failure))
1650	      }
1651	      return .failed(failure)
1652	    }
1653	    let after = await currentRevision(path: path)
1654	    return .ok(summary: Self.commitSummary(request.mode, vcs: vcs), revision: after)
1655	  }
1656	
1657	  /// A commit's ref reading and its outcome, captured together inside one gate acquisition.
1658	  private struct CommitAttempt: Sendable {
1659	    let before: String?
1660	    let result: CommandResult
1661	  }
1662	
1663	  /// The commands, in order, inside the caller's single gate acquisition.
1664	  ///
1665	  /// Returns the FIRST failing result, so the caller classifies whichever step broke. The
1666	  /// intent-to-add step only runs when the selection actually contains paths git may not know, so the
1667	  /// common case is one process.
1668	  private func runCommitSequence(_ request: VCSCommitRequest, in path: String) async
1669	    -> CommandResult
1670	  {
1671	    if vcs == "jj" {
1672	      let args =
1673	        request.mode == .describe
1674	        ? Self.jjDescribeArgs(message: request.message)
1675	        : Self.jjCommitArgs(message: request.message)
1676	      return await run(args, in: path, timeout: commitTimeout)
1677	    }
1678	
1679	    if request.mode == .amendMessage {
1680	      return await run(
1681	        Self.gitAmendMessageArgs(message: request.message), in: path,
1682	        timeout: commitTimeout)
1683	    }
1684	
1685	    // New sides only — see `gitPathspecPayload(literalPaths:)`.
1686	    let unknown = Self.pathsGitMayNotKnow(in: request.files)
1687	    if !unknown.isEmpty {
1688	      let ita = await runner.run(
1689	        vcs, Self.gitIntentToAddArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout,
1690	        stdin: Self.gitPathspecPayload(literalPaths: unknown))
1691	      guard ita.ok else { return ita }
1692	    }
1693	    let result = await runner.run(
1694	      vcs, Self.gitCommitOnlyArgs(message: request.message), in: path, timeout: commitTimeout,
1695	      stdin: Self.gitPathspecPayload(request.files))
1696	
1697	    // The commit failed, so undo the index entries we just made. Left behind, an intent-to-add marker
1698	    // is not the harmless residue it looks like: it breaks the user's own `git stash` in the terminal
1699	    // ("Entry 'x' not uptodate. Cannot merge.") until they find and reverse a change they never made.
1700	    //
1701	    // Rolled back for the untracked rows ONLY. Those were definitionally absent from the index, so
1702	    // `rm --cached` reverses exactly our own step. A rename's new side may already be a real staged
1703	    // entry (`git mv`), and unstaging that would destroy work the user did themselves — the wrong
1704	    // trade for tidiness.
1705	    if !result.ok {
1706	      let added = Self.pathsAddedToTheIndex(in: request.files)
1707	      if !added.isEmpty {
1708	        _ = await runner.run(
1709	          vcs, Self.gitUnstageArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout,
1710	          stdin: Self.gitPathspecPayload(literalPaths: added))
1711	      }
1712	    }
1713	    return result
1714	  }
1715	
1716	  /// Selected paths git may have no index entry for, which `--only` therefore cannot commit.
1717	  ///
1718	  /// Untracked files are the obvious case. The one that was missing — and that broke every commit
1719	  /// containing it — is the NEW side of a rename. `GitProvider.workingStatus` runs libgit2
1720	  /// status with `.renamesWorkingTree`, so a plain `mv old new` (what editors, IDEs and coding agents
1721	  /// all do; only `git mv` behaves otherwise) arrives as ONE `.renamed` row whose `path` is a file git
1722	  /// has never seen. `git commit --only` then fails the WHOLE selection with `error: pathspec
1723	  /// ':(literal)new.txt' did not match any file(s) known to git` — every other ticked file goes
1724	  /// uncommitted with it, and the failure classifies as `.other` with no remedy to offer.
1725	  ///
1726	  /// Including paths git already tracks costs nothing: `--intent-to-add` records no content for them,
1727	  /// so a modified tracked file stays unstaged (measured). Intent-adding the new side also lets git
1728	  /// pair the two halves itself, so the commit records a rename (`R100`) rather than an add plus a
1729	  /// delete.
1730	  static func pathsGitMayNotKnow(in files: [ChangedFile]) -> [String] {
1731	    files.filter { $0.change == .untracked || $0.change == .renamed }.map(\.path)
1732	  }

1734	  /// Of those, the ones the intent-to-add step definitely CREATED an index entry for, so a failed
1735	  /// commit can put the index back exactly as it found it.

1737	  /// Untracked rows only. Those were definitionally absent from the index, so `rm --cached` reverses
1738	  /// precisely our own step. A rename's new side may already be a real staged entry (`git mv` stages
1739	  /// the rename, and intent-to-add is then a no-op on it) — unstaging that would destroy work the user
1740	  /// did themselves, which is a far worse outcome than a leftover marker.
1741	  static func pathsAddedToTheIndex(in files: [ChangedFile]) -> [String] {
1742	    files.filter { $0.change == .untracked }.map(\.path)
1743	  }

1745	  /// Selected paths whose staged content a commit would discard, for the dialog to confirm before it
1746	  /// happens. Empty for jj, which has no index, and for a mode that takes no pathspec.
1747	  ///
1748	  /// A pre-flight rather than a refusal: a partially-staged file is a legitimate thing to commit from
1749	  /// — the user just has to know that the version on disk is the one that lands. Silence is the only
1750	  /// unacceptable option, because the loss leaves no trace (`git status` is clean afterwards).
1751	  func stagedContentAtRisk(path: String, files: [ChangedFile]) async -> [String] {
1752	    guard vcs != "jj", !files.isEmpty else { return [] }
1753	    let result = await run(Self.gitStatusPorcelainArgs(), in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
1754	    guard result.ok else { return [] }

1756	      porcelainZ: result.stdout, selecting: Set(files.map(\.path)))
1757	  }

1760	  /// nothing, and the jj form carries `jjReadFlags` so it cannot snapshot.

1763	  /// `nil != "abc123"` then reads correctly as "the ref moved".

1765	    let args = vcs == "jj" ? Self.jjOpHeadArgs() : Self.gitHeadArgs()
1766	    let result = await run(args, in: path, timeout: refTimeout)
1767	    guard result.ok else { return nil }
1768	    let value = result.stdout.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)

1770	  }

1772	  /// Which verbs each backend has. `.amendMessage` is git's and `.describe` is jj's; neither has a
1773	  /// counterpart on the other side, so a mismatch is a programming error the writer reports rather
1774	  /// than silently running the nearest command.
1775	  static func supports(mode: VCSCommitMode, vcs: String) -> Bool {
1776	    switch mode {
1777	    case .commit: return true
1778	    case .amendMessage: return vcs != "jj"
1779	    case .describe: return vcs == "jj"
1780	    }
1781	  }

1783	  static func commitSummary(_ mode: VCSCommitMode, vcs: String) -> String {
1784	    switch mode {
1785	    case .commit: return "Committed"
1786	    case .amendMessage: return "Amended the last commit"
1787	    case .describe: return "Set the change message"
1788	    }
1789	  }

1791	  /// The stderr a `committedThenFailed` carries, so the dialog can show what went wrong *after* the
1792	  /// commit landed.
1793	  static func commitFailureDetail(_ failure: VCSCommitFailure) -> String {
1794	    switch failure {
1795	    case .toolMissing(let m), .identityMissing(let m), .signingFailed(let m), .hookRejected(let m),
1796	      .unmergedFiles(let m), .sequencerInProgress(let m), .other(let m):
1797	      return m
1798	    case .timedOut: return "The command was stopped at its time limit."
1799	    case .nothingToCommit: return "Nothing to commit."
1800	    case .locked(let file):
1801	      return file.map { "Blocked by \($0.filename)." } ?? "The repository was busy."
1802	    case .unsupportedMode: return "That action isn’t available for this repository."
1803	    }
1804	  }

Based on my review, I've traced the security-relevant changes:

**Security-relevant changes analyzed:**

1. **`jjCommitArgs` / `jjDescribeArgs` — attached `--message=`** (VCSWriting.swift:841, 847): This is a **security improvement**, not a vulnerability. It closes an option-injection vector where jj's clap parser would misread a detached `-m` value starting with `-` as a flag. Verified: it's a single argv element that cannot be misparsed.

2. **`gitUnstageArgs` rollback sink** (VCSWriting.swift:592-598): New subprocess sink `git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch --pathspec-from-file=- --pathspec-file-nul`. Paths come from `pathsAddedToTheIndex(in: request.files)` (only `.untracked`). Payload uses `:(literal)` prefix and NUL separation via `gitPathspecPayload(literalPaths:)`. No shell interpolation, `--` is not needed because `--pathspec-from-file=-` reads from stdin. Safe.

3. **Whole-line `"Nothing changed."` match, scoped to jj** (VCSWriting.swift:1119-1123, 1146-1165): This closes a classification bug where a git commit whose subject contained "nothing to commit" was falsely reported as `.committedThenFailed`. Correctness fix, not a new vulnerability.

4. **Per-project commit-in-flight counter** (ProjectStore.swift:56, 66; AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift): `@MainActor` on `ProjectStore` serializes mutations. Counter decrement is paired with the Task's completion path. Not a security-sensitive sink.

5. **`gated<T: Sendable>` genericization + `before` moved inside gate** (VCSWriting.swift:1332-1336, 1633-1638): The `before`/`after` ref-comparison for `.committedThenFailed` is now taken atomically inside the gate — actually FIXES a race where a stale `before` could misclassify a genuine failure as "commit landed". Security-relevant improvement.

6. **`commitChecking` guard removal of `phase == .editing`** (CommitSheet.swift): Deliberately catches the retry-after-failure path where staged content could be silently discarded. Guard against races via `guard phase != .committing, !isSpent`.

7. **`isSpent` / `landedThenFailed` state** (CommitSheet.swift): Disables primary + secondary + escape after a landed-then-failed commit to prevent duplicate commits. Cancel disabled during `.committing` prevents dismissing a running commit (could tear down state that the completion writes into).

**No new taint→sink flows without mitigation.** The message goes as a single argv element to a subprocess (no shell); paths are NUL-separated with `:(literal)` prefix; `projectRoot` is a dictionary key, not a shell arg; the new rollback pathspec set is a subset (`.untracked` only) of the intent-to-add set. The one UX shortcoming — an intent-to-add marker left behind for a plain-`mv` rename after a failed commit — is a data-integrity tradeoff (avoiding destroying `git mv`-staged work) that the code documents explicitly. Not security.
